note: Who actually appears in the SERPs this site wants, what each one holds, and which lane it occupies. Refreshed by the daily loop. lane decides how we treat a rival, not how good they are.

lanes.retailer: Sells the same consumables we do. Contest these directly, term by term.
lanes.authority: Government, a health service, or a peak body. Do not contest the head term. A commercial page will not outrank a state health department on disposal advice and should not try. Serve the product term beside it instead.
lanes.marketplace: Amazon, eBay, Etsy and the like. Beatable on specificity and on being Australian, never on domain strength.
lanes.adjacent: Ranks in our SERPs selling something we do not and will not sell. Recorded so the gap analysis can see the whole SERP. Never a template to copy.

competitors.why: The closest thing to a direct competitor. One collection page holds insulin needles at 11,000 a month and insulin syringes at 6,500, both at difficulty 3 or lower.

A generalist supplier whose catalogue is wide enough to rank for stopwatch and panadol. Relevant to us at exactly one point: a single product page holds bacteriostatic water at 7,100 a month, difficulty 0, from position 5.

The most useful data point in this file. Domain rating 3, ranking seventh for sharps container. A page selling the thing can reach page one of a product SERP without any domain strength at all, which is the entire bet this site is making.
Holds position 2 for sharps disposal and 3 for sharps container with one resource page taking 1,678 visits a month. Not contestable on the disposal head term and not worth the attempt.
Community sharps management, position 3 and 6. A state health department. The correct response is to link to it, not to compete with it.

Position 4 for sharps container, and the brand that a long tail of our keywords is actually searching for. Around 4,000 monthly searches in the keyword file are somebody looking for a syringe at Chemist Warehouse. That is demand for a product with a shop attached to it, not demand for us, and a page that pretends otherwise is a page that bounces.
Position 8 for sharps container on a single product listing. Worth knowing because it explains the syringe bunnings long tail.
Position 6 for bacteriostatic water. Present in most product SERPs in this space.

Domain rating 0, position 2 for bacteriostatic water, 2,258 visits a month. Two facts sit in that one line. A brand new domain can take second place in this SERP, which is encouraging. And it does so as a peptide retailer, which is the one thing this business is not and will not become. We sell the same vial of sterile diluent and describe it as a diluent. Recorded as intelligence. Never as a model.

A lab instrument maker in the United States holding position 2 for needle gauge chart, on a first page that also contains a microfluidics blog, a UK reseller at domain rating 11, and a Pinterest pin about knitting needles. It looked like a vacancy until the volume came back: twenty searches a month in Australia. The page is empty because nobody local is knocking. Kept in the file as the worked example of a SERP that is weak and worthless at the same time.
